points: Q3 will reveal whether the reported freight-market tightening is translating into higher ex-fuel revenue and operating income, since Q2’s $185.2m ex-fuel revenue and $6.9m operating income were still down year over year.

The print will show if the earnings recovery is core-driven or mostly fuel-pass-through: Q2 fuel surcharge revenue jumped to $38.3m while ex-fuel revenue fell, so Q3 needs ex-fuel growth to support the long.

Management commentary on contract pricing, spot exposure and capacity constraints from CDL enforcement and the Montgomery broker-liability ruling, reports suggest, will set up Q4 and 2027 rate momentum.
Q3 operating margin and EPS will test whether the sequential rebound from Q1’s 2c to Q2’s 7c can continue toward the FY1 consensus of $0.30 and the FY2 consensus of $0.66.
The November peer prints from ODFL, WERN and HTLD will provide read-throughs, but MRTN’s own dedicated/temp and Mexico brokerage results are the main event for the long.
With the stock at a premium valuation (P/E 1.3x theme median, PEG 2.4x theme median), the Q3 print must show the 118.9% FY2 EPS growth is achievable; otherwise the multiple is vulnerable.
watch: Q3 operating income above Q2’s $6.9m — supports the long.
Ex-fuel operating revenue grows sequentially from Q2’s $185.2m — supports the long.
Operating margin expands from Q2’s ~3.1% — supports the long.
Management commentary confirms Q4 pricing/capacity tailwinds and a path toward the FY2 $0.66 EPS consensus — supports the long.
